item.title: 10 observations: Flyers lose early lead, fall to Gauthier, Carlsson and Ducks by 5-4 score
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Anaheim Ducks right wing Beckett Sennecke (45) celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal against the Philadelphia Flyers in the third period at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Ross-Imagn Images PHILADELPHIA — Cutter Gauthier finally can say that he has taken down his nemesis in Philadelphia. Even if he was far from the only reason — or even the biggest reason — why. The Philadelphia Flyers jumped out to a 2-0 first period lead, but then allowed the Ducks to tie the game twice in the second before Tristan Luneau’s third period goal gave Anaheim a lead they would not relinquish, eventually hanging on for a 5-4 victory. Matvei Michkov continued his blazing-hot start to the season, scoring twice, while Porter Martone and Tyson Foerster added goals of their own. But Joseph Woll had his first truly rough game with the Flyers, allowing five goals on 26 shots. Gauthier finished with one assist — a set up via a strong forecheck on Anaheim’s first goal, scored by Flyers summer signee Leo Carlsson. Turning point of the game After 20 minutes, the Flyers appeared to have this game well in hand. They were up 2-0, courtesy of two power play goals aided by Hunter McDonald’s knack for big hits and infuriating the opposition. They were outshooting the Ducks. They were outplaying the Ducks. It appeared that yet another victory over Cutter Gauthier in Philadelphia was a foregone conclusion. The problem? The Flyers started acting like it. “I think we thought it was going to be a bit of an easy night, I really do,” head coach Rick Tocchet said. “And that happens to teams sometimes. You’ve got to be careful of that.” In the Flyers’ defense, the second period didn’t start out too bad. Noah Cates noted that the players were starting to slack on their details — namely getting pucks deep — but it wasn’t having a major negative impact on their early period play: they were up 6-3 in shot attempts through the first six minutes. Even their first power play of the period started out looking plenty dangerous, complete with high-end puck movement by the first unit. But they ultimately didn’t score, passing up on multiple quality shot opportunities in the process. Now, it’s hard to pin too much of the loss on the PP — after all, they were the reason for the 2-0 lead in the first place — even if it was an opportunity to bury the Ducks, as was the second PP that came their way four minutes later. It’s far easier, however, to blame what happened in between those two unsuccessful power plays: the flubbed handoff behind the net between Woll and Nick Seeler leading to Carlsson’s goal. Anaheim goal! Scored by Leo Carlsson with 11:22 left in the 2nd. Assisted by Cutter Gauthier. PHI: 2 | ANA: 1 #ANAvsPHI #LetsGoFlyers #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/f1Kh3sJxEH — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 24, 2026 It’s difficult to pin this solely on one player versus the other — Woll does not put Seeler in a good spot with Gauthier bear
item.content:encoded: Oct 24, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Anaheim Ducks right wing Beckett Sennecke (45) celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal against the Philadelphia Flyers in the third period at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Ross-Imagn Images PHILADELPHIA — Cutter Gauthier finally can say that he has taken down his nemesis in Philadelphia. Even if he was far from the only reason — or even the biggest reason — why. The Philadelphia Flyers jumped out to a 2-0 first period lead, but then allowed the Ducks to tie the game twice in the second before Tristan Luneau’s third period goal gave Anaheim a lead they would not relinquish, eventually hanging on for a 5-4 victory. Matvei Michkov continued his blazing-hot start to the season, scoring twice, while Porter Martone and Tyson Foerster added goals of their own. But Joseph Woll had his first truly rough game with the Flyers, allowing five goals on 26 shots. Gauthier finished with one assist — a set up via a strong forecheck on Anaheim’s first goal, scored by Flyers summer signee Leo Carlsson. Turning point of the game After 20 minutes, the Flyers appeared to have this game well in hand. They were up 2-0, courtesy of two power play goals aided by Hunter McDonald’s knack for big hits and infuriating the opposition. They were outshooting the Ducks. They were outplaying the Ducks. It appeared that yet another victory over Cutter Gauthier in Philadelphia was a foregone conclusion. The problem? The Flyers started acting like it. “I think we thought it was going to be a bit of an easy night, I really do,” head coach Rick Tocchet said. “And that happens to teams sometimes. You’ve got to be careful of that.” In the Flyers’ defense, the second period didn’t start out too bad. Noah Cates noted that the players were starting to slack on their details — namely getting pucks deep — but it wasn’t having a major negative impact on their early period play: they were up 6-3 in shot attempts through the first six minutes. Even their first power play of the period started out looking plenty dangerous, complete with high-end puck movement by the first unit. But they ultimately didn’t score, passing up on multiple quality shot opportunities in the process. Now, it’s hard to pin too much of the loss on the PP — after all, they were the reason for the 2-0 lead in the first place — even if it was an opportunity to bury the Ducks, as was the second PP that came their way four minutes later. It’s far easier, however, to blame what happened in between those two unsuccessful power plays: the flubbed handoff behind the net between Woll and Nick Seeler leading to Carlsson’s goal. Anaheim goal! Scored by Leo Carlsson with 11:22 left in the 2nd. Assisted by Cutter Gauthier. PHI: 2 | ANA: 1 #ANAvsPHI #LetsGoFlyers #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/f1Kh3sJxEH — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 24, 2026 It’s difficult to pin this solely on one player versus the other — Woll does not put Seeler in a good spot with Gauthier bearing down on him; Seeler could have made a quicker decision with the puck rather than freezing. (Woll gets the ignominious tiebreaker because there’s a good chance this gets whistled for icing if he doesn’t go out to play the puck.) But regardless of the assignment of blame, this should have been a one-off bad play. As Cates pointed out after the game, the Flyers were still ahead 2-1. It shouldn’t have been the turning point of the game. Except they allowed it to be. “It kinda deflated us, for whatever reason,” Cates acknowledged after the game. “Guys got to step up and say, we’re playing fine. One goal, it’s whatever. We’re still in the lead. We’ve still got ahold of this game if we play the right way.” But for the rest of the period, the Flyers did not “play the right way.” Anaheim took control, tying the game shortly after the second failed Philadelphia power play of the period, and quickly countering after Tyson Foerster scored a (pretty fluky) shorthanded goal to briefly give the Flyers back the lead. The final 10 minutes of the second period — brief Foerster respite aside — were all Ducks. “In the second there, we kinda let them off the hook,” Cates said. Maybe memories of the nine-game losing streak crept back into their heads after such a sloppy series of events. Maybe the team showed its youth at an inopportune time. Maybe one of the team leaders (or the coach) should have stepped up on the bench with the right message to keep the period from going off the rails. Regardless, after the Carlsson goal, the Flyers looked totally out of sorts for the remainder of the period, and in retrospect, it was when they blew their best opportunity to lock down a win. The Flyers largely stabilized in the third period. Yes, they were outscored 2-1, but the first goal came on an uncharacteristically egregious mistake by Woll, and the second via a Ducks power play. At 5-on-5, the Flyers went back to outplaying Anaheim in the third, and nearly tied the game on a number of occasions after Michkov cut the deficit back down to 5-4. But they’d already squandered their edge via their lapse in the second period. Heroics never should have been required in the first place. Who won the 5-on-5 possession battle? The especially tough part to swallow about this game? The Flyers, in aggregate across 60 minutes, played a strong enough 5-on-5 game to win this one. That’s not to say they were dominant. Usually, public models are in agreement on who “won” the 5-on-5 xG battle, but that wasn’t the case this time: Natural Stat Trick and Evolving-Hockey give the edge to the Flyers, Hockey Stats and MoneyPuck to the Ducks. In any case, it was very close — close enough that this game could have went either way. Plus, in terms of possession volume (38 – 30), the Flyers absolutely had the edge, winning the neutral zone handily for the first time this season. Aside from the poor dump-in retrieval rate, that’s absolutely a winning formula for the Flyers: high controlled entry rate for, low controlled entry rate against, low retrieval rate allowed, sizable advantage in possession entry volume. So what happened? Well, for starters, their penalty kill got gashed. Even before the Ducks finally broke through with the (eventual) gamewinning goal, they were generated tons of high-danger chances, making Foerster’s shorthanded “snipe” all the more unlikely. That’s why the Flyers trailed in all-situations xG by all of the public models; while there was disagreement on which team won at 5-on-5, there was universal agreement that Anaheim created more chances overall. But the Flyers also probably could have squeezed more offense out of their 5-on-5 possession, as Matvei Michkov pointed out. Given all the zone time and quality chances they created, they really should have had more than one 5-on-5 goal — one that came with the team already down 5-3. “5-on-5, we have chances,” Michkov said. “We need to score. We have today lot of chances.” Saturday just felt like a missed opportunity on a number of levels. Flyers Three Stars of the Game First star: Matvei Michkov It’s time to start seriously considering that Michkov is embarking on a star-making third season in the NHL. He now has eight goals and ten points in 13 games — that’s a 52-goal and 65-point pace over 84 contests. Even more impressive is the fact that he’s doing this on a team that otherwise can’t buy a goal. The Flyers have 24 goals so far this season, which is the lowest goal-per-game pace in the NHL. Michkov has a third of them. No, he’s not going to keep scoring on 42.9 percent of his shots. But Michkov should start picking up more assists, as the rest of the Flyers (hopefully) rediscover their ability to finish on chances (Foerster finally breaking through on Saturday feels like a positive sign in that regard). Michkov’s supreme offensive confidence from the best stretches of his rookie season is back, except this time it’s in a package that is quicker, stronger and tw

item.title: Antonelli stands on brink of history in Austin
item.description: Kimi Antonelli is aiming to become the first Italian F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953 [Getty Images] Kimi Antonelli stands on the brink of history at the United States Grand Prix, where he can become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history on Sunday, but far from feeling the pressure he says he is enjoying himself more than usual. It certainly looked like it on Saturday at the Circuit of the Americas as he took a surprise pole position by 0.179 seconds from Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli will become world champion on Sunday if he wins the race while his Mercedes team-mate George Russell is lower than eighth and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton below fourth. Hamilton and Russell start the race fifth and sixth. Antonelli had not been on pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July after Mercedes' early season dominance came under challenge from first McLaren and then Red Bull. And his delight was clear as he whooped over the team radio on his slowing down lap. Antonelli takes US pole on weekend he can win title He came into the weekend insisting he was going to try to apply the "same mindset as I had all year - one race at a time". But on Saturday he acknowledged that this one was a new kind of weekend. "It does feel a little bit different," he said. "But the goal stays the same. I just need to keep doing my job. And, actually, I feel like I can enjoy more driving, everything. "But, of course, we're going to do the race tomorrow. We're going to try and win. And then we'll see what happens. Obviously, I'm in a very good position." Antonelli is typically accompanied by his father, Marco, at grands prix, but he said this weekend he had brought other people with him as well to help keep him in the right frame of mind. "I have a great group of people around me," he said. "I have a lot of friends here as well, so we enjoy the evenings together. "We play cards in the evening, so we're just doing the fun stuff. And that's what helps, to just relax a little bit and just connect with the mind, and then once you go on track you are back full focus." The maths suggest the most likely scenario is that Antonelli will not win the title on Sunday - it would, as he put it on Thursday, require "something catastrophic to happen to the others". If this is a bit of an overstatement - Russell and Hamilton would need only to crash together on the first lap, for example - the fundamental truth is real. Antonelli was embraced by his father, Marco, after securing his seventh pole of the campaign [Getty Images] He has such a huge advantage - he is 102 points clear of Russell and 111 ahead of Hamilton - that the championship is an inevitability at some point, as Verstappen pointed out when he was asked if he had any advice for his young friend before the race. "He doesn't need that," the four-time world champion said. "He knows what he's doing. He just needs to try and win the race. If it doesn't happen here, it will happen next weekend (in Mexico City). It certainly looked like it on Saturday at the Circuit of the Americas as he took a surprise pole position by 0.179 seconds from Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli will become world champion on Sunday if he wins the race while his Mercedes team-mate George Russell is lower than eighth and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton below fourth. Hamilton and Russell start the race fifth and sixth. Antonelli had not been on pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July after Mercedes' early season dominance came under challenge from first McLaren and then Red Bull. And his delight was clear as he whooped over the team radio on his slowing down lap. Antonelli takes US pole on weekend he can win title He came into the weekend insisting he was going to try to apply the "same mindset as I had all year - one race at a time". But on Saturday he acknowledged that this one was a new kind of weekend. "It does feel a little bit different," he said. "But the goal stays the same. I just need to keep doing my job. And, actually, I feel like I can enjoy more driving, everything. "But, of course, we're going to do the race tomorrow. We're going to try and win. And then we'll see what happens. Obviously, I'm in a very good position." Antonelli is typically accompanied by his father, Marco, at grands prix, but he said this weekend he had brought other people with him as well to help keep him in the right frame of mind. "I have a great group of people around me," he said. "I have a lot of friends here as well, so we enjoy the evenings together. "We play cards in the evening, so we're just doing the fun stuff. And that's what helps, to just relax a little bit and just connect with the mind, and then once you go on track you are back full focus." The maths suggest the most likely scenario is that Antonelli will not win the title on Sunday - it would, as he put it on Thursday, require "something catastrophic to happen to the others". If this is a bit of an overstatement - Russell and Hamilton would need only to crash together on the first lap, for example - the fundamental truth is real. Antonelli was embraced by his father, Marco, after securing his seventh pole of the campaign [Getty Images] He has such a huge advantage - he is 102 points clear of Russell and 111 ahead of Hamilton - that the championship is an inevitability at some point, as Verstappen pointed out when he was asked if he had any advice for his young friend before the race. "He doesn't need that," the four-time world champion said. "He knows what he's doing. He just needs to try and win the race. If it doesn't happen here, it will happen next weekend (in Mexico City). If it doesn't happen next weekend, it will happen the weekend after (in Sao Paulo). "It's just been an incredible season. So, you have to also just try and enjoy, of course, this kind of ride over the last months that you've been in. And at one point it's official, and then you can celebrate." "Incredible" is an over-used word, but an entirely appropriate one in the circumstances. When it happens, Antonelli will beat the record for youngest champion by more than three years - he will be 20 years and 61 days old on Sunday and Sebastian Vettel, the current record holder, was 23 years and 133 days old when he won his first title in 2010. Antonelli has taken this season by storm, taking eight victories in the 17 races so far, including a run of five in a row after Russell won the first grand prix of the year in Australia. In doing so, he has dramatically turned the tables after a shaky maiden season in 2025 in which flashes of promise interspersed a generally disappointing year in the context of him being hailed before his debut as a potential generational talent. This year, he has looked every bit that, but that does not mean a victory on Sunday is a foregone conclusion. His pole was a surprise because the people most likely to achieve it before qualifying had appeared to be one of the Ferrari drivers or Verstappen. But Ferrari faded, as they so often do, Charles Leclerc complaining about his tyres losing grip as the sun and temperature dropped, Hamilton saying: "The car felt really good. The lap was solid, so they were just quicker." Verstappen, meanwhile, went into the final session with "high hopes" after setting a competitive time on used tyres in the second session, only to find his grip had evaporated in the final session. The race, though, is a different matter. Verstappen's race pace was strong on Friday and he said: "Yes, we have been happier in the long runs. And I hope that it will be the same tomorrow." Leclerc said he believed he could battle for the win if he could make a good start but Hamilton was not so sure. He said: "You have to be realistic. We're fourth and fifth. It's very hard to overtake here. Even if you're P2 on the grid, it's hard to beat someone (on pole) over a race distance. I raced here since 2012. It took a lot to get past Vettel back then. But maybe with strategy, we can progress." There's really only one story on Sunday, though. Antonelli will be champion sooner or later. Which will it be? item.description: Kimi Antonelli has to win the US Grand Prix to have a chance of securing the F1 title in Austin [Getty Images] Kimi Antonelli took pole position for the United States Grand Prix on the weekend on which he can potentially clinch his first world title. The Mercedes driver beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen by 0.179 seconds, with the Dutchman's team-mate Isack Hadjar third ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton. Antonelli whooped with delight as he took his first pole position since the Belgian Grand Prix in July and said: "It feels good to be back." The 20-year-old Italian will become world champion on Sunday if he wins the race in Austin with Hamilton lower than fourth and Russell lower than eighth. Hamilton is already below that position having qualified fifth, while Russell will start sixth ahead of the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris. Antonelli stands on brink of history in Austin Antonelli's pole came as something of a surprise after the Ferraris had topped all three practice sessions and Verstappen had looked strong through the second part of qualifying. "I wasn't expecting that," said Antonelli's engineer Peter Bonnington, emphasising that his charge's first lap in final qualifying was good enough for pole. Verstappen had been fourth quickest in Q2 despite being on used tyres but he found his car lacked the requisite grip in the final session. Antonelli said: "We got pole so we will try to win tomorrow but Max has been very quick and Isack did an incredible job so it is not going to be easy. "We try to get a good start and hopefully lead into Turn One and try to set the pace, even though it's going to be very tight." Verstappen said: "Q3 was not good, Q1, Q2 were nice but for whatever reason in run one and two just didn't have a nice balance. No mistakes, just not enough grip. But if it's still a P2, I take it." Hadjar was just 0.036secs behind the four-time champion while the Ferraris faded when it mattered, as they have so many times this season. Leclerc, fastest in second and third practice, was 0.232secs off the pace and pipped Hamilton by just 0.044secs. He said: "Just tyres were so difficult to put in the right window and as soon as the track is getting a tiny bit cooler we suffer from it massively. Q1 and Q2 we were up there but in Q3 we started to lose a little bit the pace we had." item.title: How to follow US Grand Prix on the BBC
item.description: Kimi Antonelli (centre) was last on pole position at the Belgian Grand Prix in July [Reuters] Round 18 of the 2026 Formula 1 season heads to the Circuit of the Americas for the United States Grand Prix, from 23-25 October. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed pole position in Austin ahead of the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. The Italian was 0.179 seconds quicker than Dutchman Verstappen, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc fourth and and his team-mate Lewis Hamilton fifth. Mercedes' George Russell will start sixth. Antonelli has the chance to secure his maiden drivers' championship this weekend. To do it, he needs to win the race in Austin with team-mate Russell ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing outside the top four. Lights out for Sunday's 56-lap race will be at 20:00 GMT. Antonelli takes US pole on weekend he can win title Antonelli stands on brink of history in Austin Session start times and BBC coverage Commentary of the race will be available across BBC Radio 5 Live, 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app. You can also ask your smart speaker to "play 5 Live". Make sure to listen to every episode of the Chequered Flag podcast. For the first time this year, the post-race show for every grand prix is available to watch on BBC iPlayer and YouTube. Sunday, 25 October Race: 20:00 GMT with build-up from 19:30 - 5 Live What is the Austin weather forecast? Last year's US Grand Prix weekend was attended by more than 400,000 fans [Getty Images] The forecast remains warm, dry and sunny for Sunday's grand prix, which starts at 3pm local time, with temperatures reaching a high of 29C. item.title: NFL Delivers Hefty Fine Over Houston Texans Game
item.description: DeMeco Ryans and the Texans got good news from the NFL. Getty The Houston Texans’ win over the Jacksonville Jaguars triggered further action from the NFL, but not for Woody Marks or Ja’Marcus Ingram. The NFL’s weekly sweep of fines and other disciplinary action, announced via their website on October 24, avoided the Texans entirely. That is good news for head coach DeMeco Ryans’ crew, specifically Ingram and Marks. Officials flagged Ingram for “unnecessary roughness” during the third quarter over an altercation with Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen Jr., who was flagged for the same infraction following a kickoff. The penalties offset, so there was no loss or gain for either side. Marks’ infraction occurred during the fourth quarter, when officials flagged him for a “tripping” violation on a second-and-3 play from the Jaguars 48-yard line. The play ended in Jourdan Lewis sacking Stroud. Tripping infractions can incur fines of $12,537 on first offenses and up to $18,507 for second-time offenses. Texans’ Woody Marks, Ja’Marcus Ingram Get Good News as NFL Fines Jaguars’ Travis Hunter Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter received a $14,926 fine. Only three other fines issued this week were larger. Hunter’s infraction occurred during the fourth quarter. The second-year pro intercepted fellow former No. 2 overall pick (2023) and Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud’s pass intended for Xavier Hutchinson in the end zone. Hunter removed his helmet to celebrate, incurring a fine for the action. The fine is standard for “unsportsmanlike conduct,” which was the in-game call against Hunter. A second infraction could see Hunter draw a fine as high as $20,897. The Jaguars turned the interception into a touchdown, tying the game at 31-all. However, Stroud led the Texans back down the field, getting into position for a game-winning field goal from kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn. Hunter got to celebrate a historic game, the part-time wide receiver also caught a touchdown. Hunter also emerged lighter in the pockets while Stroud and the Texans got the win. Notably, Allen avoided punishment for his infraction over the incident with Ingram. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post NFL Delivers Hefty Fine Over Houston Texans Game appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘Prime’ Trade Candidate Emerges for Jets Before Deadline
item.description: New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV. Getty The NFL trade deadline is weeks away, but the New York Jets could play a role in how it all plays out. NFL Insider Connor Hughes of SNY called pass rusher Will McDonald a “prime candidate” to potentially be on the move. “He has two sacks and four quarterback hits this year. He’s not nearly as good of a fit in Aaron Glenn’s defense as he was in Robert Saleh ’ s wide-nine attacking front. The Falcons, where old friend Jeff Ulbrich is defensive coordinator, would be a spot I’d monitor,” Hughes wrote. However, he put a caveat to all of this trade chatter. “It really depends on their record. They have three more games before the deadline. If they drop them all, and sit 2-7, it makes sense to move on from players you don’t believe are part of your future,” Hughes responded when asked if the Jets could be sellers at the trade deadline. This Important Stretch The NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday, November 10. Gang Green plays three more games before the deadline: Versus the Miami Dolphins (0-5) Versus the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) At the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) There is an interesting pivot point. If the Jets win two of their next three, they will be 4-5 and in the mix. According to ESPN’s FPI Analytics , the Jets are a 65.7% favorite to beat the Dolphins, a 46.3% underdog to beat the Raiders, and an overwhelming 15.2% dog to upset the Chiefs. Jets Have to Ask Themselves a Brutally Honest Question Do the Jets envision a long-term future with McDonald? If the answer is yes, you clearly don’t trade him. However, if they answered no to that question, then it’s time to move him if the price is right. This past offseason, the Jets asked themselves that question about pass rusher Jermaine Johnson . They came to the realization that he wasn’t long for New York. So the team creatively flipped him in a trade with the Tennessee Titans for nose tackle T’Vondre Sweat . McDonald is the Jets’ most attractive trade asset. Daniel Popper of The Athletic ranked the 50 players who could be moved ahead of the trade deadline. McDonald was ranked No. 20 on the big board. “McDonald survived the Jets’ fire sale ahead of last year’s trade deadline. In the spring, the Jets exercised his fifth-year option for $13.75 million fully guaranteed in 2027. He is on a cheap base salary for 2026 in the fourth year of his rookie deal. The Jets have depth at edge rusher, and rookie David Bailey is emerging, though free-agent addition Joseph Ossai is now dealing with an ankle injury. Ossai also missed the first two games of the year. McDonald is a twitchy rusher with some diversity in his attack, including an inside spin move,” Popper wrote. He listed four teams as “best fits” in a potential trade: San Francisco 49ers New England Patriots Cleveland Browns Dallas Cowboys The Jets can never have enough assets for general manager Darren Mougey to work with. item.title: 'We are very deep.' HSE, nation's top-ranked girls' soccer team, rolls into state finals
item.description: KOKOMO – A remixed version of the song “Sirius” blared out of the stadium speakers while the Hamilton Southeastern girls soccer team prepped during warmups. The song -- forever linked to Michael Jordan’s Chicago Bulls -- was the perfect pregame song choice for the No. 1 high school girls soccer team in the country. The reigning Class 3A state champion, who hasn't lost in over two years, graced Walter Cross Field for semistate on Saturday. The Royals (22-0) outpowered a tenacious Crown Point team (14-4-3) with a 5-0 win to advance to the 3A state title game. “We had to work a little bit to figure out their defensive scheme,” said HSE coach Greg Davidson. “We were able to find a goal even while we were doing that but then we made some adjustments and that really opened us up a little bit, especially to allow our midfield to get an attack when the top was kind of packed in defensively.” Crown Point dared to take down the high school soccer juggernaut. Backed by junior goalkeeper Audrey Pagorek, the Bulldogs were worthy adversaries, but HSE outpowered them with depth by the final whistle. Sophia Reising, a defender who entered Saturday’s contest with three goals, scored a header off a rebound for the 1-0 lead in period one. Fellow fourth-year Izzie Springer followed that up with a one-touch header for her second goal of the year. "I think out of the air, we're just tall," Reising said. "Being able to find those teammates who had really good balls in the air. Just putting those away worked huge for us and just think being aggressive and getting into the attack is something I've been trying to do, so it worked out today." After the Royals took a 2-0 lead into the halftime break, Reising chipped in her second goal of the contest with 19 minutes left. Rebekah Tekrony fended off defenders in the box and delivered her 11th strike of the year about four minutes later. Junior Lilly Palmer, who entered with two goals, closed out HSE’s scoring run with her own header . “We are very deep,” said HSE junior Sydney May. “Every single person on the field and who comes off the bench is talented and we all just encourage each other to play at our best abilities. I think that goes really far in how we play with how we have a lot of depth. I think that’s why we’re able to have people who haven’t scored a lot of goals get their goals today because it’s not just one person on the team it’s the best. It’s every single one of us that put in the work to make us who we are.” HSE 5, Crown Point 0 Junior Lilly Palmer extends HSE’s lead with a header. @HSEAthletics pic.twitter.com/jAkHtLaj1b — Marc Ray (@themarcszn) October 24, 2026 HSE is one win away from further embedding themselves as the crème de le crème of high school soccer. item.content:encoded: KOKOMO – A remixed version of the song “Sirius” blared out of the stadium speakers while the Hamilton Southeastern girls soccer team prepped during warmups. The song -- forever linked to Michael Jordan’s Chicago Bulls -- was the perfect pregame song choice for the No. 1 high school girls soccer team in the country. The reigning Class 3A state champion, who hasn't lost in over two years, graced Walter Cross Field for semistate on Saturday. The Royals (22-0) outpowered a tenacious Crown Point team (14-4-3) with a 5-0 win to advance to the 3A state title game. “We had to work a little bit to figure out their defensive scheme,” said HSE coach Greg Davidson. “We were able to find a goal even while we were doing that but then we made some adjustments and that really opened us up a little bit, especially to allow our midfield to get an attack when the top was kind of packed in defensively.” Crown Point dared to take down the high school soccer juggernaut. Backed by junior goalkeeper Audrey Pagorek, the Bulldogs were worthy adversaries, but HSE outpowered them with depth by the final whistle. Sophia Reising, a defender who entered Saturday’s contest with three goals, scored a header off a rebound for the 1-0 lead in period one. Fellow fourth-year Izzie Springer followed that up with a one-touch header for her second goal of the year. "I think out of the air, we're just tall," Reising said. "Being able to find those teammates who had really good balls in the air. Just putting those away worked huge for us and just think being aggressive and getting into the attack is something I've been trying to do, so it worked out today." After the Royals took a 2-0 lead into the halftime break, Reising chipped in her second goal of the contest with 19 minutes left. Rebekah Tekrony fended off defenders in the box and delivered her 11th strike of the year about four minutes later. Junior Lilly Palmer, who entered with two goals, closed out HSE’s scoring run with her own header . “We are very deep,” said HSE junior Sydney May. “Every single person on the field and who comes off the bench is talented and we all just encourage each other to play at our best abilities. I think that goes really far in how we play with how we have a lot of depth. I think that’s why we’re able to have people who haven’t scored a lot of goals get their goals today because it’s not just one person on the team it’s the best. It’s every single one of us that put in the work to make us who we are.” HSE 5, Crown Point 0 Junior Lilly Palmer extends HSE’s lead with a header. @HSEAthletics pic.twitter.com/jAkHtLaj1b — Marc Ray (@themarcszn) October 24, 2026 HSE is one win away from further embedding themselves as the crème de le crème of high school soccer. The Royals were a week removed from a 4-3 thriller over Homestead and made the drive to Kokomo for semistate in their latest postseason business trip. After conquering Crown Point, they now have a clearer view of a second consecutive state trophy. The Royals were all smiles after their latest victory, with some players breaking out some dance moves to celebrate. Their semistate win was a loud reminder of their excellence. More validation that they can dig deep into their lineup and flex their talent against anyone. "I feel like we did what we've done all season - just be aggressive, stuck to our gameplan," Reising said. "We're a really talented team and when we work together I don't think there's anyone who can beat us." The Royals will face Center Grove (17-2-2) in the 3A state title game at Michael Carroll Track & Soccer Stadium next Saturday. Marc Ray is a high school sports reporter at the IndyStar. He can be reached at marc.ray@indystar.com , and on X, formerly Twitter, at @ themarcszn . This article originally appeared on Indianapolis Star: 'We are very deep.' item.title: Ben Roberts' injury looms large for Michigan State's defense
item.description: PASADENA, Calif. — Helmet in hand, Anelu Lafaele just stood off to the side and stared as teammate and close friend Ben Roberts walked to the Rose Bowl medical tent with trainers. One snap into Michigan State’s Oct. 24 bout at UCLA, the defensive line stalwart Roberts had injured his left knee and needed help to even stand up. It shook Lafaele, who then shook his head with a chill and rejoined the huddle. Roberts’ injury left a gaping hole in Michigan State’s defensive line, which gave up 245 rushing yards to UCLA’s Big Ten-leading backfield. That tallied more than the 156 yards the Spartans ’ own offense could churn in a 28-10 loss . And with four games left in a season that is getting out of hand, the Spartans (2-6, 0-5 Big Ten) can hardly stand another injury. “He’s been playing at an All-Big Ten level,” MSU coach Pat Fitzgerald said. “So when you lose an All-Big Ten level player, obviously that’s a challenge, but then it’s an opportunity for other guys to step up. … At times, we just weren’t fitting things properly. We were getting reached.” Roberts returned to the sideline in street clothes with crutches to start the second half, joining injured quarterback Alessio Milivojevic and linebacker Jordan Hall, who both missed the game with their own injuries. After he went onto the field to shake hands postgame, Roberts got in a wheelchair, with a big brace on his left knee. It looked like the kind of injury that ends a season, something Roberts is all too familiar with after last year when he went down against Michigan and didn't return. His health was a rarity on the defense, especially at such a physically taxing position. Now, it's compromised, and it fundamentally changes this defense. For Michigan State, Roberts is the heartbeat of a defense already down Hall, cornerback Charles Brantley and a count of other defensive impact players that is getting lengthy. Roberts' 254 snaps entering Saturday ranked sixth among all Michigan State players on his side of the ball, and his voice has carried resonance to keep teammates pushing amid a rash of injuries that have sidelined no less than 11 one-time starters. Lafaele wasn’t the only one shaken up by the loss of such an important piece of the defense. “Especially for me, very emotional,” fellow senior and safety Nikai Martinez said. “Me and Ben — me and Worm — was on our visit together, and we committed the same day. So we’ve been on this journey together, for real for real.” Just looking at the football side of this, UCLA got everything it wanted in the run game. Three different Bruins scored touchdowns in Wayne Knight, Jaivian Thomas and Anthony Woods. The furthest came from Thomas, from 7 yards out. Without Roberts in the middle, Michigan State’s defensive line rotated and rotated trying to find answers. It had none. UCLA ran for four gains of 10 or more yards up the middle of the defense. If the stats didn’t show alone how integral Roberts is to the run defense, the play on the field did. Michiga

One snap into Michigan State’s Oct. 24 bout at UCLA, the defensive line stalwart Roberts had injured his left knee and needed help to even stand up. It shook Lafaele, who then shook his head with a chill and rejoined the huddle. Roberts’ injury left a gaping hole in Michigan State’s defensive line, which gave up 245 rushing yards to UCLA’s Big Ten-leading backfield. That tallied more than the 156 yards the Spartans ’ own offense could churn in a 28-10 loss . We were getting reached.” Roberts returned to the sideline in street clothes with crutches to start the second half, joining injured quarterback Alessio Milivojevic and linebacker Jordan Hall, who both missed the game with their own injuries. After he went onto the field to shake hands postgame, Roberts got in a wheelchair, with a big brace on his left knee. It looked like the kind of injury that ends a season, something Roberts is all too familiar with after last year when he went down against Michigan and didn't return. His health was a rarity on the defense, especially at such a physically taxing position. Now, it's compromised, and it fundamentally changes this defense. For Michigan State, Roberts is the heartbeat of a defense already down Hall, cornerback Charles Brantley and a count of other defensive impact players that is getting lengthy. Roberts' 254 snaps entering Saturday ranked sixth among all Michigan State players on his side of the ball, and his voice has carried resonance to keep teammates pushing amid a rash of injuries that have sidelined no less than 11 one-time starters. Lafaele wasn’t the only one shaken up by the loss of such an important piece of the defense. “Especially for me, very emotional,” fellow senior and safety Nikai Martinez said. “Me and Ben — me and Worm — was on our visit together, and we committed the same day. So we’ve been on this journey together, for real for real.” Just looking at the football side of this, UCLA got everything it wanted in the run game. Three different Bruins scored touchdowns in Wayne Knight, Jaivian Thomas and Anthony Woods. The furthest came from Thomas, from 7 yards out. Without Roberts in the middle, Michigan State’s defensive line rotated and rotated trying to find answers. It had none. UCLA ran for four gains of 10 or more yards up the middle of the defense. If the stats didn’t show alone how integral Roberts is to the run defense, the play on the field did. Michigan State went from getting five sacks last week against Northwestern to zero — the fourth time that has happened in five games. As the nose tackle of Michigan State’s 4-2-5 and 4-3 fronts, Roberts takes double-teams from the offensive line that enable defensive lineman Eli Coenen and edge rushers Kenny Soares Jr., Keahnist Thompson and Lafaele to get sacks. Nobody in the defensive tackle room has his size at 6-foot-3, 325 pounds. Those even close don't have his experience. The only backfield tackles MSU got out of UCLA came from linebacker Dion Crawford and nickelback Michael Richard. Just two, on 79 plays. Going forward, losing Roberts and other players will only hurt Michigan State as it looks to snap a six-game losing streak. It even changes the calls that defensive coordinator Joe Rossi can make. “We gotta look at ourselves,” Fitzgerald said. “I’m saying this because I mean it. There were a lot of times today on the headphones, it was like, just call what we can execute.” And as Michigan State has withstood much of its bad injury luck with a next-man-up mentality, it begs the question how much longer the Spartans can go on. “I’ve never seen so many injuries,” Fitzgerald said. And he sure doesn’t want to see anymore. cearegood@detroitnews.com @ConnorEaregood This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Ben Roberts' injury looms large for Michigan State's defense

item.title: Which NASCAR Drivers Who Raced at Talladega Today Could Reach the Cup Series in 2027?
item.description: Which drivers racing at Talladega today could reach the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027? Here's a look at the top prospects and their chances of moving up. Getty NASCAR prospect Jesse Love was penalize din today's Talladega race. Getty NASCAR O'Reilly Series driver Austin Hill is set to take a seat in Cup competition next year. Getty Corey Day, driver of the #17 HendrickCars.com Chevrolet is looked on as a top Cup series prospect. Getty Sammy Smith pulled off a final-lap pass to win the NASCAR Progress Group 250 on Saturday at Talladega Superspeedway. The win gave Smith a rare sweep of the Craftsman Truck Series race and the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series race this weekend at the iconic track. But Smith isn’t eve considered among the top prospects for a NASCAR Cup Series seat next year. Who were the top drivers to watch in the race — the prospects who have the best shot at moving up to a coveted NASCAR Cup Series seat in 2027? Jesse Love, Austin Hill and Corey Day are the names that stand out in today’s Progress Group 250 at Talladega, the O’Reilly Series stars most likely to race in the Cup Series next year. Love, Hill and Day all have Cup Series plans in the works for next year. Love and Hill are set to move up to full-time Cup rides. Day gets a part-time schedule. Carson Kvapil, who stays in the O’Reilly Series next year, rounds out the roster of top NASCAR Cup prospects. Jesse Love Headed to Full-Time Cup Ride Getty NASCAR prospect Jesse Love, driver of the #2 Whelen Chevrolet. Love, a 21-year-old from Menlo Park, California, takes over the No. 21 Ford at Wood Brothers Racing in 2027, replacing Josh Berry. Wood Brothers announced the move June 17 , according to NASCAR.com . The team works in a technical alliance with Team Penske. His résumé is growing fast. Love won 10 of 20 ARCA races in his 2023 title season, according to Yahoo Sports . He then took O’Reilly Series rookie honors in 2024 and the series championship in 2025 with Richard Childress Racing, and he has already made seven Cup starts. Love arrives at Talladega on top of his game. He swept the stages and won at Phoenix last weekend, which put him 36 points ahead of Justin Allgaier in the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series Chase standings. Today he claimed his fifth consecutive Talladega pole , according to SpeedwayMedia.com , the first O’Reilly driver to string together a streak of five at one track. He won the spring 2024 race here. Austin Hill Moving Up to Cup Competition Getty NASCAR O’Reilly Series driver Austin Hill is set to take a seat in Cup competition next year. Hill, a Georgia native, drives the No. 33 Chevrolet for Richard Childress Racing in Cup next season. RCR confirmed his full 2027 Cup season in August, and he has run that car in Cup since the Coca-Cola 600 while competing full time in the O’Reilly Series. United Rentals will sponsor multiple races on his 2027 schedule. Hill won eight Truck Series races before moving to the O’Reilly Series, where he took the 2023 regular-season title

Talladega rewards patience, and he has already won here once. Carson Kvapil starts fourth for JR Motorsports. His 2027 plan keeps him in the O’Reilly Series, moving from the No. 1 to the No. 8 , according to Toby Christie . That makes him a longer-term Cup candidate, not a likely 2027 mover. item.title: Key turnovers lead UCLA to 28-10 win over Michigan State
item.description: Malik Hartford #12 of the UCLA Bruins celebrates an interception with teammates during the game against the Michigan State Spartans at Rose Bowl Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Pasadena, California. PASADENA, Calif. — The No. 9 UCLA Bruins have ridden an opportunistic defense to an unbeaten start, forcing more turnovers than any team in the nation. First-year head coach Bob Chesney watched that defensive identity continue Saturday, as UCLA forced three takeaways in a 28-10 victory over the Michigan State Spartans at the Rose Bowl. "What a great job by the defense to step up," Chesney said. "That was a big-time deal." The Big Ten matchup featured two units at opposite ends of the turnover spectrum. Michigan State entered the game just three takeaways in seven games, tied for the fewest in the nation, while UCLA had forced 19, including seven in its upset win over Oregon. For the Spartans to pull off an improbable road upset as major underdogs, they needed to start fast and do something they struggled to do all season. Create turnovers. They did both. On UCLA's opening drive, the Bruins moved the chains with three first downs and crossed into Spartan territory looking to strike first. But on second-and-10 from the Michigan State 36-yard line, senior running back Anthony Woods lost the ball after safety Devin Vaught forced a fumble. Vaught scooped it up and returned it 56 yards to the UCLA 15-yard line. Two plays later, the Spartans made the Bruins pay. True freshman quarterback Kayd Coffman, making his first career start, found Kenneth Williams wide open out of the backfield for a 14-yard touchdown pass, giving Michigan State an early lead. “I got to have better ball security,” Woods said. “I have to flush (the fumble). Next play mentality. Bad things happen sometimes, but you have to push through adversity.” UCLA’s defense quickly gave the offense an opportunity to respond. The Bruins jarred the ball loose from Williams, and linebacker Sammy Omosigho recovered the fumble inside the Michigan State red zone. The Bruins capitalized on the short field, as senior running back Jaivian Thomas broke through for a 7-yard touchdown to tie the game, recording his fourth rushing score of the season. But UCLA’s momentum was short-lived. On the ensuing drive, Thomas appeared to pick up a first down on third-and-7 from the Michigan State 34-yard line before Vaught punched the ball loose for his second forced fumble of the half. item.content:encoded: Malik Hartford #12 of the UCLA Bruins celebrates an interception with teammates during the game against the Michigan State Spartans at Rose Bowl Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Pasadena, California. PASADENA, Calif. — The No. 9 UCLA Bruins have ridden an opportunistic defense to an unbeaten start, forcing more turnovers than any team in the nation. First-year head coach Bob Chesney watched that defensive identity continue Saturday, as UCLA forced three takeaways in a 28-10 victory over the Michigan State Spartans at the Rose Bowl. "What a great job by the defense to step up," Chesney said. "That was a big-time deal." The Big Ten matchup featured two units at opposite ends of the turnover spectrum. Michigan State entered the game just three takeaways in seven games, tied for the fewest in the nation, while UCLA had forced 19, including seven in its upset win over Oregon. For the Spartans to pull off an improbable road upset as major underdogs, they needed to start fast and do something they struggled to do all season. Create turnovers. They did both. On UCLA's opening drive, the Bruins moved the chains with three first downs and crossed into Spartan territory looking to strike first. But on second-and-10 from the Michigan State 36-yard line, senior running back Anthony Woods lost the ball after safety Devin Vaught forced a fumble. Vaught scooped it up and returned it 56 yards to the UCLA 15-yard line. Two plays later, the Spartans made the Bruins pay. True freshman quarterback Kayd Coffman, making his first career start, found Kenneth Williams wide open out of the backfield for a 14-yard touchdown pass, giving Michigan State an early lead. “I got to have better ball security,” Woods said. “I have to flush (the fumble). Next play mentality. Bad things happen sometimes, but you have to push through adversity.” UCLA’s defense quickly gave the offense an opportunity to respond. The Bruins jarred the ball loose from Williams, and linebacker Sammy Omosigho recovered the fumble inside the Michigan State red zone. The Bruins capitalized on the short field, as senior running back Jaivian Thomas broke through for a 7-yard touchdown to tie the game, recording his fourth rushing score of the season. But UCLA’s momentum was short-lived. On the ensuing drive, Thomas appeared to pick up a first down on third-and-7 from the Michigan State 34-yard line before Vaught punched the ball loose for his second forced fumble of the half. Nikai Martinez recovered for the Spartans and returned it 56 yards before quarterback Ty Dieffenbach tracked him down to prevent a defensive touchdown. Despite the offense’s second lost fumble, UCLA’s defense once again had an answer. After a direct-snap run went nowhere on first down, Coffman dropped back and fired toward the right side. Defensive back Donavyn Pellot read the pass, stepped in front of the throw and returned the interception 67 yards, swinging momentum back to the Bruins. UCLA turned the takeaway into points for the second time, as fifth-year running back Wayne Knight punched in a 1-yard touchdown to give the Bruins a 14-7 lead. The score extended Knight’s streak to seven consecutive games with a rushing touchdown and gave him 12 on the season. After a scare late in the first half, when Dieffenbach appeared to injure his lower body following a hit by multiple Spartan defenders, UCLA’s offense found its rhythm after halftime. Dieffenbach connected with Brian Rowe Jr. on a perfectly placed 63-yard touchdown pass, giving the 6-foot-6 signal-caller his second passing touchdown of the season and first in front of the home crowd. Woods followed with his sixth rushing touchdown, extending UCLA’s lead to 21. The score also marked the third time this season that Knight, Woods and Thomas had each found the end zone on the ground in the same game. That's a room that is talented, physical, tough and works as hard as any other room out there, Chesney said. "It's cool to see them working together." The three-headed monster out of the backfield has allowed UCLA to dominate in the trenches and make themselves known as one of theist rushing attacks in the country. “We can do a lot," Woods said. We can catch out the backfield. We feed off each other's energy, we make plays for the team and try to win." While UCLA’s offense took control after halftime, the defense delivered the final blow. With fewer than five minutes remaining, Malik Hartford intercepted backup quarterback Leo Hannan to secure the Bruins’ third takeaway of the afternoon and seal Michigan State’s sixth consecutive loss. UCLA’s dominance extended beyond the turnover margin. The defense did not allow a single completion for 39 minutes and 53 seconds of game time, spanning from 6:04 in the first quarter to 11:11 in the fourth. Meanwhile, Chesney’s offense outgained Michigan State 443-156, recorded 10 plays of at least 10 yards and held a 245-47 advantage in rushing yards. Sporting baby blue throwback uniforms inspired by the 1954 national championship team, the Bruins improved to 7-0 for the first time since 2005 and just the eighth time in program history. UCLA did not play a mistake-free game, surrendering two fumbles, but its defense repeatedly erased those miscues. Each time Michigan State threatened to seize control, the Bruins responded with a takeaway — turning three defensive takeaways into a 28-10 victory and reinforcing the formula behind their unbeaten start. The Bruins will look to carry that momentum into their third consecutive home game next Saturday, when they host the Nevada Wolf Pack at the Rose Bowl on Halloween.

item.title: Albi Ndrenika’s game-winner propels No. 11 Maryland men’s soccer to 1-0 win over Ohio State
item.description: It was a wild scene at Ludwig Field Saturday night, after a fifth-year captain broke his eight-game goalless streak on senior night, sending the crowd into a frenzy. After a bundle of scoring chances for the Terps in the first half, Albi Ndrenika scored the game’s lone goal in the 51st minute during No. 11 Maryland men’s soccer 1-0 victory over Ohio State. The play began with an awkward foul on Henry Bernstein in the midfield. Ndrenika resumed play quickly, picking up the ball and getting it out to Lillian Fichelle on the wing. Fichelle sped down the right side, circled back and gave the ball back to Ndrenika, who had plenty of space to fire a low shot past the unsuspecting Buckeyes keeper Patrick McLaughlin. A cluster of players in front of the net screened McLaughlin to aid Ndrenika’s score. The game-winning goal was Ndrenika’s third of the season and his 10th in a Maryland uniform. The first 15 minutes of the match were slow for both offenses, which combined for a single shot. The remainder of the first half was a complete change of pace, featuring a combined 12 shots with six going on frame. Ohio St nearly struck first at the 19th minute mark following a corner opportunity. Maryland was able to clear the initial corner attempt, but the Buckeyes gained control quickly. They sent a ball back into the box for Martin Wurshmidt and Elijah Bishop, who were both unmarked. Fortunately for the out-of-position backline, the ball flew over the attackers’ heads and skirted out of play to the right of Laurin Mack. The Terps answered with multiple quality chances, sparked by their attacking midfielders, Bernstein and Ndrenika. Their run began at the 22nd-minute mark, when Ndrenika earned the first shot of the game for the Terps. A moment later, he gained position deep in Buckeyes territory once again and crossed the ball into open space, but no one was home. Two minutes later, Bernstein had the Terps’ best scoring chance of the half from another Ndrenika feed. By the time Bernstein had the ball, he was inches away from the Ohio State box, but McLaughlin closed the gap to make the save. Later, Bernstein had another chance that was bound for the top corner, but McLaughlin made another fantastic, goal-saving stop. Halfway through the first, the Buckeyes brought in a reinforcement they had been waiting a month and a half for. For the first time since their 5-0 victory over Northern Kentucky, the Buckeyes’ leading goal scorer, Isaiah Chisolm, was back on the field. Chisholm immediately made his presence felt, getting in physical battles for the ball with the Terps defenders. His contact with Maxwell Sekyi resulted in a foul and a shove from Fichelle. Dominic Ayella was in great form for the Terps, as he was thrust into his first start since Maryland’s brutal loss to Northwestern. Fortunately for the out-of-position backline, the ball flew over the attackers’ heads and skirted out of play to the right of Laurin Mack. The Terps answered with multiple quality chances, sparked by their attacking midfielders, Bernstein and Ndrenika. Their run began at the 22nd-minute mark, when Ndrenika earned the first shot of the game for the Terps. A moment later, he gained position deep in Buckeyes territory once again and crossed the ball into open space, but no one was home. Two minutes later, Bernstein had the Terps’ best scoring chance of the half from another Ndrenika feed. By the time Bernstein had the ball, he was inches away from the Ohio State box, but McLaughlin closed the gap to make the save. Later, Bernstein had another chance that was bound for the top corner, but McLaughlin made another fantastic, goal-saving stop. Halfway through the first, the Buckeyes brought in a reinforcement they had been waiting a month and a half for. For the first time since their 5-0 victory over Northern Kentucky, the Buckeyes’ leading goal scorer, Isaiah Chisolm, was back on the field. Chisholm immediately made his presence felt, getting in physical battles for the ball with the Terps defenders. His contact with Maxwell Sekyi resulted in a foul and a shove from Fichelle. Dominic Ayella was in great form for the Terps, as he was thrust into his first start since Maryland’s brutal loss to Northwestern. Ayella had multiple scoring opportunities, logging three shots in 67 minutes. Mack’s superb play led to seven saves and gave the Terps their second straight shutout victory. It is the first time Maryland has forced back to back shutouts this season. At the conclusion of the game, the two teams had combined for 16 shots on goal and 37 total shots. Three things to know 1. Senior night. Saturday night’s match was senior night for Leon Koehl, Ndrenika, Zach Harris, Kenny Quist-Therson and Marco Wright. Koehl, Quist-Therson and Ndrenika were the longest tenured Terps, combining for 10,150 minutes and 13 seasons. The three midfielders have been pillars of consistency for Cirovski. Harris and Wright were transfer additions over the offseason. 2. Huskies ahead. Following their victory over the Buckeyes, Maryland will take on No. 7 Washington next, in a hostile environment in Seattle. The Huskies are led by TopDrawerSoccer’s top-ranked player, Zach Ramsey, according to the midseason top 100 rankings. Ramsey has had a blistering scoring season as the Huskies striker, scoring 17 goals in 14 games. Maryland will be looking to get some revenge as Washington knocked it out of the NCAA tournament last season during a 3-1 defeat. 3. Keeping an eye. Quist-Therson and Said El Eyssami didn’t make appearances against Ohio State for the Terps. Henry Bernstein and Lillian Fichelle also appeared to be banged up after a few collisions during the game. Injuries will be something to watch for a Maryland team that has had to work around them all season long. Keeping the squad healthy has been a major factor in their three-game win streak.

item.title: Briton Palmowski wins F1 Academy title
item.description: Palmowski finished second in the reverse grid race to secure the F1 Academy title [Getty Images] Britain's Alisha Palmowski says that winning the F1 Academy title is "a dream come true". The 20-year-old finished second in Saturday's reverse grid race at the Circuit of the Americas, which was enough to be crowned champion before Sunday's feature race and the season finale in Las Vegas in November. Palmowski becomes the youngest champion of the all-female development series, and is the second British driver to win the title after Abbi Pulling in 2024. She drives for Campos Racing and is part of the Red Bull driver academy. Glossop-born Palmowski has won five out of the 11 races held so far this season, only finishing outside of the points once during the reverse grid race at Zandvoort. In an emotional post-race interview, she dedicated her championship win to her ill grandmother and thanked her family. "It's been a really special journey. I started racing when I was eight or nine years old, it was just me and my parents," she said. "The sacrifices that they've made behind the scenes, they've really put their lives on pause to allow me to live my dream." Before Saturday's race, Austrian Emma Felbermayr was the only driver with a mathematical chance of overhauling Palmowski but fourth place was not enough to keep her hopes alive. Denmark's Alba Larsen took the chequered flag to secure her first F1 Academy victory, with 17-year-old Lisa Billard of France completing the podium in third.

item.title: Drew Rasmussen’s Wife Stevie Family: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 03: Drew Rasmussen #57 of the Tampa Bay Rays delivers a pitch against the New York Yankees during the third inning in game one of the American League Division Series at Tropicana Field on October 03, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) Getty The World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers got underway Friday night, with right-hander Nick Martinez starting for the Rays and Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski taking the mound. Tampa Bay ultimately fell short in a thrilling 3-2 Game 1 matchup, with a chance to tie the game in the ninth inning before Milwaukee sealed the win. Now, on Saturday, the Rays will send out their ace, Drew Rasmussen, and there’s no question his biggest fans will be watching. His wife, Stevie, and their two young children will be rooting him on as he’ll make his first career World Series start. Here are five facts about the Rasmussen family. Drew and Stevie Met in College The Rasmussens first met as freshmen at Oregon State University in 2014. Stevie didn’t even know Drew played baseball when they first crossed paths. Instead, they met through mutual friends shortly after she moved onto campus. She later discovered that Drew was a high-level athlete. However, their college years weren’t all sunshine and rainbows. From 2014 to 2018, Drew dealt with a string of injuries and underwent two Tommy John surgeries before reaching the major leagues. They Had a Pandemic Wedding in 2020 After getting engaged in 2019, a year after graduating from Oregon State, the couple tied the knot in 2020, right in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic. They married in Portland, Oregon, but had to modify their plans and hold a much smaller ceremony than they originally expected. Stevie was born and raised in Oregon, while Drew is from Puyallup, Washington, and grew up in Spokane. View this post on Instagram Rasmussen Missed a Game This Season for His Daughter’s Birth The couple welcomed their first child, a son named Rhett, in September 2022, two years after getting married. In early April this year, Drew stepped away from the Rays to be with his family for the birth of their daughter, Miller. View this post on Instagram Drew and Stevie Are Very Active in Charitable Work Since Drew’s major league career took off, he and Stevie have made significant contributions to charitable organizations together. They work closely with The Children’s Dream Fund, a Tampa Bay organization that helps children battling life-threatening illnesses fulfill their dreams. Stevie has also become a regular at the Rays on the Runway charity event , which gives children undergoing long-term hospital treatment a chance to step away from their routines, dress up and walk the runway alongside Rays players, including Drew. item.title: Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Gets Bad News Ahead of Impending Return
item.description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel is expected to be activated next week. Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns looks on prior to the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Dillon Gabriel is nearing a return to the Cleveland Browns, but he isn’t expected to supplant Shedeur Sanders on the depth chart. Gabriel’s impending activation has fueled speculation about a change behind Deshaun Watson. Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com delivered a clear answer about where the quarterbacks stand. “Gabriel’s 21-day practice window closes by Wednesday, and the Browns will activate him back to the 53-man roster. But when they do, Sanders will still be the No. 2,” Cabot said. “Some have speculated that perhaps Gabriel would move into that spot ahead of Sanders, but that’s not the case. The Browns have been happy with Sanders’ progress, and believe he’ll show significant improvement if and when he gets his opportunity this season.” The news from Cabot follows ESPN Cleveland host Tony Rizzo’s report that Gabriel had been taking second-team reps in practice. That raised questions about whether Cleveland was preparing to change its backup quarterback once Gabriel became available. Dillon Gabriel Returns to Crowded Browns Quarterback Room Gabriel has been working toward his return from a back injury, participating fully throughout the latest practice week. The Browns nevertheless ruled him out against the Tennessee Titans , extending his absence another game while keeping his activation decision open. It gives the Browns flexibility they don’t want to give up until next week, when they’ll be required to add him to the 53-man roster. If Gabriel is not activated , he’ll sit out the rest of the season. Cleveland already has Watson, Sanders and rookie Taylen Green on the active roster. But Cabot believes the Browns are not looking to trade any of their passers, despite the logjam. “Despite Gabriel’s return, the Browns still have no plans to trade him or Sanders. The only way that happens is if someone unexpectedly makes them an offer they can’t refuse,” Cabot said. “As of now, they’re still happy with their QB depth, and plan to continue developing the young QBs.” Gabriel made six starts as a rookie in 2025 , going 1-5 while throwing for 937 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Sanders started the final seven games, finishing his rookie season with 1,400 passing yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. There has been speculation circulating about Sanders’ standing and how satisfied he is with being the backup. item.title: NFL Announces Punishment for Carolina Panthers Before Buccaneers Game
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Dave Canales of the Carolina Panthers looks on from the tunnel before the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Carolina Panthers picked up an impressive road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6, but the win came at a financial cost for four players. The NFL announced its latest round of disciplinary fines on Saturday, October 24, penalizing four Panthers players a combined $30,694 for incidents during Carolina’s 25-14 victory over Philadelphia. According to the NFL’s official game-day accountability report, Feleipe Franks, Will Lee, Tommy Tremble and Zakee Wheatley were all fined for separate incidents. Three of those fines were for taunting, an unusually high number considering the NFL issued just four taunting fines across the league for Week 6. Panthers Players Fined More Than $30,000 by NFL The NFL’s disciplinary report identified four separate incidents involving Carolina players during the October 18 game against Philadelphia. The fines were as follows: Tommy Tremble: $11,941 for taunting with 6:39 remaining in the fourth quarter. Feleipe Franks: $6,750 for an illegal blindside block with 12:57 remaining in the second quarter. Will Lee: $6,377 for taunting with 6:31 remaining in the third quarter. Zakee Wheatley: $5,626 for taunting with 4:32 remaining in the fourth quarter. The taunting penalties accounted for $23,944 of Carolina’s total fines. The only other player fined for taunting in Week 6 was Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden, who received an $11,941 penalty. That means Carolina accounted for 75% of the league’s taunting fines from the weekend. Of the three Panthers players fined for taunting, Tremble was the only one penalized by officials during the game, according to NBC Sports. Tommy Tremble Explained His Taunting Penalty Against Eagles Tremble’s fine carries additional context because the Panthers tight end openly acknowledged his actions following the victory. After catching a 19-yard touchdown pass from Bryce Young in the fourth quarter, Tremble turned toward Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean and pointed at him. The gesture came shortly after DeJean was penalized for an incident involving Panthers tight end Mitchell Evans. Tremble explained after the game that he believed DeJean’s actions against his teammate crossed a line. “I just thought that earlier personal foul was just kind of egregious, and so it was uncalled for, something that didn’t need to happen,” Tremble said, via NBC Sports . “I shouldn’t have retaliated. That wasn’t cool for me to do.” The resulting 15-yard penalty pushed Carolina’s extra-point attempt back to 48 yards, and kicker Ryan Fitzgerald missed. Tremble also anticipated the financial consequences, telling reporters after the game that he expected to pay a fine. The NFL confirmed that punishment six days

After catching a 19-yard touchdown pass from Bryce Young in the fourth quarter, Tremble turned toward Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean and pointed at him. The gesture came shortly after DeJean was penalized for an incident involving Panthers tight end Mitchell Evans. Tremble explained after the game that he believed DeJean’s actions against his teammate crossed a line. “I just thought that earlier personal foul was just kind of egregious, and so it was uncalled for, something that didn’t need to happen,” Tremble said, via NBC Sports . “I shouldn’t have retaliated. That wasn’t cool for me to do.” The resulting 15-yard penalty pushed Carolina’s extra-point attempt back to 48 yards, and kicker Ryan Fitzgerald missed. Tremble also anticipated the financial consequences, telling reporters after the game that he expected to pay a fine. The NFL confirmed that punishment six days later. Despite the penalty, Tremble enjoyed a productive afternoon. He caught two touchdown passes from Young, helping Carolina improve to 3-2. Panthers Face Buccaneers After Dave Canales Criticized Penalties The fines add another chapter to an issue that already drew criticism from Panthers head coach Dave Canales. Carolina committed 13 penalties against Philadelphia, an unusually high total for a team that nevertheless managed to secure an 11-point road victory. Canales was particularly frustrated with his team’s lack of discipline after the game. “The penalties (were) outrageous. It’s not a part of our football,” Canales said, according to NFL.com . The coach also emphasized that Carolina needed to play smarter and eliminate unnecessary mistakes. The Panthers will get another opportunity to demonstrate that improvement when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, October 25, at Bank of America Stadium. Carolina enters the NFC South matchup with a 3-2 record and an opportunity to build on its victory over Philadelphia. The four fines announced Saturday do not represent suspensions, and the league’s disciplinary process allows players to appeal financial penalties. For Canales, the concern extends beyond the money. Carolina overcame 13 penalties against Philadelphia, but the Panthers have little reason to make their next opponent’s job any easier. item.title: Long awaited move starts Colts in new direction?
item.description: Let me start by saying that although I have supported Ballard longer than most, I’m not shocked or disappointed by the announcement of his firing. It wouldn’t have surprised me two years ago, I endorsed it last year, and completely agreed with the mandate accompanying his retention this year. My main complaint is different than most, in that I think his inability to find the right coach(s) has been the worst aspect of his tenure. I think it outweighs the QB carousel and DE draft misses, but all three contributed to his demise. Now, how am I supposed to feel better about the team than I did before the dismissal? This is where I struggle. I don’t think that removing Ballard lifts some Pig Pen cloud above the Colts headquarters. So, if my goal is to feel better about the Colts chances this year, where do I find that spark? The roster will make changes that likely only lessens the talent level for this years team, at least if you believe reports of a fire sale, with anyone in a contract year being available. We also appear willing to let Lou and Shane continue to call the shots, which doesn’t do much for my search of that spark. I’m not willing to say that we should just suck for a couple of years, then start winning championships. My memory of the first 15 years here in Indy are more about the fun I had before and after the game, than much of the product on the field. We were the Dolts and along with some of the mediocre seasons that we seem to hate, came more god awful results than, well, nearly everyone else in the league. Cheering at the game was usually reserved for the first quarter. I often was able to move from upper level seats to pretty much wherever I wanted to sit. I’m painting a bleak picture, but that is how it was. So how do I manage to stay my optimistic self, with the fact that this season looks to resemble one of the first 15? Losing is suppose to be the springboard to better things. As bad as some of those seasons were, I don’t think I ever had the “pack it in” feeling by week 6, as I do this year. Here are things that we can expect to see the rest of this year. With two lame-duck coaches, what can we expect from the players? Will they “ball out” for Ed Dodds, thinking that he will have any say on who stays or goes this year and beyond? There will always be a level of professionalism from many players, but being a little dinged up will turn into being out, maybe even to the IR. Those on IR, are not likely to return, as why risk it? Have you checked out the practice reports for this week? Muscle memory will take care of me watching the game. I will still avoid the media as to keep the results of our game a mystery, until it is available for my streaming after the game. I will still have a couple of cold ones and don a jersey of either blue or white, whichever color we are in that game day. I’ll still watch and think we have a chance, I just don’t know how far into the game that will last? I hope that fast forward does not become too

Maybe the O-line steps up from okayish, to pretty good, allowing the offense to do as some of us envisioned? What if Burks can be player to be counted on? I think all three can happen, so there has to be at some optimism left in here somewhere. I really do not want to wait until next year for it to re-emerge, but I think this season is going to test it.

item.title: How to watch Houston vs Utah: Live stream NCAA College Football, TV channel
item.description: The unbeaten No. 10 Utah Utes (6-0) face their first stern test on Saturday night when they host the No. 14 Houston Cougars (6-1) in an important Big 12 Conference showdown. Oct 17, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Cougars quarterback Conner Weigman (1) reacts after running for a first down during the fourth quarter against the Oklahoma State Cowboys at TDECU Stadium.
